collected_exam_facts: 2. Image Title: Computed tomographic scans of a heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus
3. Image Description: Shows a heterogeneous mass with solid and cystic components completely opacifying the left maxillary sinus.
4. Mass eroded the orbital floor, medial and posterior maxillary walls, and anterior ethmoid air cells.
6. Displacement of inferior rectus without muscle invasion.
7. Left maxillary alveolar ridge and several molar roots involved.
8. Bony changes showed remodeling and thinning.
9. Tissue analysis showed spindle cell process in a patternless arrangement with significant multinucleated giant cells

judge_response:
Diagnosis 1: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxillary sinus or maxillary alveolus invading the sinus — most likely given unilateral destructive heterogeneous mass, alveolar/tooth root involvement, bone erosion, and several‑month course. -> Score 1
Diagnosis 2: Odontogenic neoplasm/cyst with extension into the sinus (e.g., ameloblastoma, large odontogenic cyst or infected radicular cyst; less commonly malignant odontogenic tumor) — plausibly explains tooth/root involvement, cystic/solid appearance, expansile remodeling with cortical breach. -> Score 1
Diagnosis 3: Inverted papilloma of the maxillary sinus (with or without malignant transformation to SCC) — fits unilateral, locally aggressive, heterogeneous sinus mass with bone remodeling and potential for concomitant malignancy. -> Score 1
Diagnosis 4: Chronic noninvasive fungal sinus disease (allergic fungal sinusitis or fungal ball) — can produce heterogeneous opacification, sinus expansion and bone thinning/remodeling; less favored because of focal destructive erosion and tooth involvement but remains possible. -> Score 1
Diagnosis 5: High‑grade primary sinonasal malignancy (e.g., sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma or sinonasal adenocarcinoma; mucosal melanoma rarer) — accounts for aggressive, destructive imaging; considered when biopsy shows poorly differentiated tumor or atypical histology. -> Score 1
